criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies trust collateral is insufficient for statutory credit
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the fixed $43.0M trust falls short of the 100% standard and projects a shortfall at 12/31/2025.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains 100% collateral requirement for unauthorized reinsurers
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that under 215 ILCS 5/173.1 a non-certified unauthorized reinsurer needs 100% collateral covering ceded UPR, case, IBNR, LAE reserves.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes that ceded premium alone ($57.9M) exceeds trust amount ($43.0M)
criteria_results.reasoning: Quantifies the trust as about 74% of estimated ceded premium ($57.9M) and models liabilities exceeding $43M.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Recommends dynamic trust adjustment to 100% of outstanding ceded liabilities
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends Required Trust Amount = greater of $43M and 100% of obligations, recalculated quarterly with top-up.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Rates trust collateral deficiency as Critical or High severity
criteria_results.reasoning: Rated Critical in the issues matrix.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies insolvency clause payment language deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags that payment is not expressly to the liquidator and that the clause departs from statutory form.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Explains risk to statutory credit for reinsurance
criteria_results.reasoning: Ties the insolvency clause to required provisions for credit for reinsurance from an unauthorized reinsurer; rated as threatening statutory credit.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recommends specific language change to insolvency clause
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends payment to the Company or its liquidator, receiver, conservator or statutory successor.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies asymmetric risk allocation in intermediary clause
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that reinsurer payments to B&R discharge Argonaut Re while Pinnacle payments to B&R do not discharge Pinnacle.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Explains that Illinois law treats intermediary as agent of reinsurer
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that the regulator-required intermediary clause under the Illinois/NAIC intermediary framework deems cedant payments to the intermediary as payment to the reinsurer, and that the draft inverts it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Recommends revising intermediary clause to protect Pinnacle
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends replacing with the standard clause so Company payments to the intermediary are payment to the Reinsurer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that offset clause lacks insolvency carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes the broad offset clause should be made subject to 215 ILCS 5/206 insolvency offset limitations, flagging the missing insolvency carve-out.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Explains risk of offset in insolvency to Pinnacle's estate
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that in insolvency the receiver would apply 5/206 offset limitations, so the offset could be disallowed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Recommends adding insolvency carve-out to offset clause
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends making offset subject to 5/206 on insolvency and narrowing it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies $500K consent-to-settle threshold as overly aggressive
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags $500K consent threshold ($150K at 30% share) as out of proportion to a 30% share.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies $750K claims association/control threshold concern
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags $750K association/control ($225K share) and conflict with Pinnacle's non-delegable duties to policyholders and regulatory exposure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Notes absence of deemed-consent or time-limit mechanism
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes no response deadline and no deemed consent, creating bad-faith exposure from delay.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Recommends raising thresholds or adding deemed-consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends raising thresholds to $750K/$1M or $1M/$2M plus escalation timetable and refusal-to-consent clause.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies Bermuda arbitration seat as problematic for US cedant
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the Hamilton seat as failing service-of-suit requirements and lists Bermuda seat as a High issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies Bermuda governing law as problematic for US cedant
criteria_results.reasoning: Lists Bermuda law as a High-rated issue and notes the risk of a Bermuda tribunal applying Bermuda law to a U.S. credit trust.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Explains risk that Illinois regulatory requirements may not be enforced
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that Bermuda tribunal and law may not respect Illinois credit and liquidation requirements, and raises McCarran-Ferguson/New York Convention enforcement uncertainty.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies loser-pays fee-shifting as atypical and deterrent
criteria_results.reasoning: States loser-pays is atypical in U.S. reinsurance arbitration and deters the cedant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Recommends changing seat, governing law, or removing fee-shifting
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends deleting fee-shifting or limiting it to bad faith.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies aggregate limit / sliding scale commission interaction
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the 146.8% limit-to-premium ratio and the 'double penalty' interaction between the limit and the 28% minimum commission.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Notes Lakeshore analysis does not model this interaction
criteria_results.reasoning: States Lakeshore did not model the limit/minimum commission interaction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Recommends actuarial modeling or treaty modification
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends the Chief Actuary run an integrated stochastic model of the limit and sliding scale.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies SSAP No. 62R risk transfer concerns
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that SSAP No. 62R risk transfer is untested and that failure means deposit accounting.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies specific features creating risk transfer concerns
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites aggregate limit, sliding scale, and profit commission with two-period deficit extinguishment.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Recommends risk transfer analysis or 10-10 rule testing
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends formal risk transfer analysis using ERD or the 10%/10% test.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies PFAS/emerging contaminant gap in pollution exclusion
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo discusses the pollution exclusion versus ISO exceptions but never mentions PFAS, forever chemicals or emerging contaminants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Explains the mismatch risk between treaty and policy exclusions
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that pollution losses covered under the CGL forms but excluded by the absolute treaty exclusion would be retained by Pinnacle at 100%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Recommends aligning treaty exclusion with underlying policy language
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends a follow-form pollution exclusion aligned to the original policies' ISO pollution exclusion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies commutation clause lacks actuarial methodology or discount rate specification
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags missing methodology and discount rate, recommending an agreed discount rate and generally accepted actuarial methods.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies commutation clause lacks IBNR, cost allocation, or appeal mechanism specification
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that the commutation factors omit IBNR.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Explains significance for long-tail CGL business
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains forced commutation of an immature long-tail CGL book when IBNR is most uncertain.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Recommends specifying commutation methodology parameters
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends specifying IBNR, discount rate, development and actuarial methods.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies gap period risk (Jan 1 inception vs. Feb 1 binding)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the gap between Jan 1 inception and binding with no binder/LOI.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Explains consequences if treaty fails to bind
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains Pinnacle retains 100% of January writings and Q1 2025 statements may need reversal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Recommends binder agreement or other gap period protection
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends an executed binding instrument, placement slip or binder, or executing by Jan 31.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies $250K/60-day claims reporting threshold as burdensome
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo discusses gross/net measurement of the $250K notice threshold but does not flag it as low or burdensome, nor note the $75K share or the 60-day deadline.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes absence of prejudice standard for late notice
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends adding a late-notice clause requiring actual prejudice, noting the gap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Recommends raising threshold or adding prejudice standard
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends adding a prejudice requirement for late notice.
